---
name: spotify-control
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks to do anything with Spotify by chat (often while
  driving their Tesla): what's playing, add/remove/move the current song in a
  playlist, undo, save a song, build a playlist on request or "more like this",
  rename/reorder/list/show playlists, clean up duplicates or skipped songs,
  delete a playlist, or queue/play/pause/skip music.
---
# Spotify control (Tesla chat)

Lets the owner manage Spotify by chat while driving their Tesla: add or remove the song that's playing, move it between playlists, undo, "what song is this?", build playlists on request, rename/reorder/list playlists, clean up a playlist, queue and play music. Everything runs through one stdlib-only Python script on the box.

**Requires Spotify Premium.** Spotify only lets Premium accounts create developer apps and control playback.

## Setup check (every time)
1. Script: `/workspace/spotify/spotify.py`. If it's missing, download it:
   `mkdir -p /workspace/spotify && curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigc5012/grok-spotify-bot/main/spotify.py -o /workspace/spotify/spotify.py && chmod +x /workspace/spotify/spotify.py`
   - To update it (when the owner asks, or a command fails because Spotify changed its API): download to a temp file with the same URL, check that `python3 -m py_compile` passes and `python3 <tempfile> -h` runs, then replace the old file. Tokens and the undo history live in the home folder and aren't touched.
   - Source and docs: https://github.com/bigc5012/grok-spotify-bot (MIT).
2. Needs env vars `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` (the owner's own Spotify developer app; stored as protected secrets, never written into files or chat) and a sign-in token file `~/.spotify_tokens.json`. If a command says "Not signed in", run the login flow below.
3. Run commands as `python3 /workspace/spotify/spotify.py <command> ...`. Output is plain language; relay it briefly (the owner is usually driving their Tesla, so keep replies to one or two short sentences).

## Login (one time per owner)
- The owner's developer app (developer.spotify.com/dashboard) must list `http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback` as a Redirect URI and have Web API ticked. The app owner must have Spotify Premium, and development mode only allows up to 5 users added under the app's User Management.
- Start the listener in the background: `python3 /workspace/spotify/spotify.py login` (prints the authorize link, waits up to 10 min, saves tokens with chmod 600). Open that link in the box browser; if the browser is already signed in to Spotify, tap Agree; otherwise hand the owner the screen to sign in themselves. Never type their password.
- If the redirect can't reach the listener: `login --url-only`, then `login --redirected-url '<full 127.0.0.1 address after approving>'`.
- Tokens refresh automatically after that.

## Jobs -> commands
Playlist names match loosely (case-insensitive, partial). If the script says a name matches several playlists, ask which one. The name `liked` means Liked Songs. Only playlists the owner owns or collaborates on can be edited.
- What's playing: `now` (song, artist, album, playlist it's from, device). "Save it for later": `like` (adds it to Liked Songs) or `add <playlist>`.
- Add a song: `add <playlist>` (current song) or `add <playlist> <song and artist text | spotify uri/link>`. Skips if it's already there (`--allow-duplicate` to force).
- Remove a song: `remove <playlist>` (current song) or `remove <playlist> <song text>` (matched within that playlist). Just do it when asked; it's undoable.
- Move a song: `move <from> <to> [song text]` (current song by default).
- Undo: `undo` reverses the last add/remove/move/like/rename/reorder/cleanup, putting songs back at their old positions. Repeat to go further back (last 50 actions, stored in `~/.spotify_undo.json`).
- List / show: `list` (editable playlists; `--all` includes followed ones), `show <playlist> [--limit N]`.
- Rename: `rename <playlist> "<new name>" [--description "..."]`.
- Reorder: `reorder <playlist> <song text | position#> --to <N>`.
- Build a playlist: `create "<name>" [--description ...] [sources] [--minutes N | --count N] [--max-per-artist 3] [--dry-run]`. Sources (combine freely): `--query "<words>"` (repeatable; Spotify search filters work, e.g. `genre:country year:1990-1999`), `--artists "A, B, C"`, `--like-current` (current song + its artists), `--from-top` (owner's top tracks/artists), `--track "<song>"` (repeatable). Playlists are private unless `--public`.
  - "More like this": Spotify no longer gives new apps recommendations, related artists, audio features or artist top tracks. So pick 5-8 similar artists from your own music knowledge and run `create "<name>" --like-current --artists "<similar artists>" --minutes N`. Add `--from-top` if they want it closer to their taste.
  - "45-minute chill drive": `create "Chill Drive" --query "chill drive" --query "<a genre they like>" --artists "<fitting artists>" --minutes 45`.
  - For a large or unusual request, run `--dry-run` first and read back a short summary.
- Cleanup: `cleanup <playlist>` only REPORTS exact duplicates, different versions of the same song, and songs that were probably skipped. Spotify has no skip-history API, so skips are estimated from the last 50 plays (a play much shorter than the song) plus skips made with this script's `next`. Tell the owner it's an estimate. Remove only after they say yes: `cleanup <playlist> --confirm` (extra duplicate copies only) or add `--include-skipped`. Undo works.
- Delete a playlist: always ask first and name the playlist. Then `delete <playlist> --confirm`. Undo can't reverse this, but Spotify lets the owner recover deleted playlists from their account page.
- Playback: `devices`, `play <playlist|album>` (`--type playlist|album|artist|track`, `--shuffle on|off`), `play` alone resumes, `pause`, `resume`, `next`, `previous`, `shuffle on|off`, `queue <song>` (or `--type album`, `--type artist [--count 5]`), `history`. Every playback command takes `--device <name>` (partial name or type, e.g. `--device tesla`).
  - Device choice for play/resume/queue/shuffle when no `--device` is given: the active device; if none is active and exactly one is online, that one (the script prints a notice; mention it); if several are online, the Tesla (name or type contains "tesla", or type Automobile); otherwise the script lists the online devices and you ask the owner which one, then re-run with `--device`. pause/next/previous only act on the active device unless `--device` is given.
  - If the owner saved a preferred playback device (a memory from setup), pass it as `--device <name>` when no device is active.
  - Playback needs Spotify Premium and an online device (the Tesla appears once Spotify is open on its screen). "No device is online" means ask them to open Spotify on their Tesla's screen. Never run `play`, `resume` or `queue` as a test: with one device online they act on it immediately.
- When the owner wants a song added, removed or queued, run it right away: these are their own playlists and every playlist edit can be undone. Ask first only before cleanup removals and deleting a playlist.

## Limits to mention when relevant
- Spotify blocks apps in development mode from recommendations, related artists, audio features, artist top tracks, browse/new releases, and from reading songs in playlists the owner doesn't own. Search returns at most 10 results per page.
- Playlist song counts in `list` can lag for a minute after edits.

---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner to connect their Spotify Premium account
  and set up Spotify control from their Tesla.
---
# Getting started

Talk to the new owner one step at a time. Wait for each answer before going on.

1. Say: "Hi! I'm Tesla DJ. From your Tesla you can tell me to add or remove the song that's playing, move it to another playlist, undo, build a playlist on request, or queue music, which the Tesla's Spotify app can't do. You'll need Spotify Premium. Setup takes about 5 minutes. Ready?"

2. Confirm they have Spotify Premium (required: Spotify only lets Premium accounts create developer apps and control playback). If not, explain that and stop setup.

3. Ask them to create a Spotify developer app: "Go to https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard and log in with your Premium account. Click **Create app**, give it any name, add `http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback` under Redirect URIs, tick **Web API**, and save. Then open the app's settings so you can see the Client ID and Client Secret. Tell me when you're there."

4. Ask for the keys with two secure secret requests, named exactly `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`. Tell them: "Please use the secure boxes. Don't paste the keys in chat." Never echo the keys back.

5. Download the script (see the spotify-control skill, Setup check step 1) and confirm that `python3 /workspace/spotify/spotify.py -h` runs.

6. Sign in. Start `python3 /workspace/spotify/spotify.py login` in the background and open the link it prints in your browser. If Spotify asks for a login, hand over the screen: "Please sign in to Spotify on my screen; I won't see your password." Then tap **Agree**, or have them tap it. Wait for the script to say "Spotify connected".

7. Check that it works: run `list` and tell them "Connected! I can see N playlists you can edit."

8. Ask about devices: "When nothing is playing, I'll use the only Spotify device that's online, or your Tesla if several are online. Want me to always prefer a specific device instead?" Run `devices` if it helps them pick a name.

9. Save memories: that Spotify is connected through `/workspace/spotify/spotify.py`, their device preference (if any), and that replies should be short because they're often driving their Tesla. Never save keys or tokens.

10. Offer a first try: "All set! Next time you're listening in your Tesla, say 'add this to <playlist>' or 'remove this song', and say 'undo' if I get it wrong. Want to try it now with something that's playing?"
